chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: Other labels and the honking show-business routine
summary: Philo, the Messner brothers' label, and the honking tenor battle with J.D. King that Howard McGhee staged.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: [HEARTY LAUGH] Yeah... So that's how I really got started into the recording thing. Later on I recorded some things for the Philo label, which was Norman Granz's early label. That was short for Philharmonic, right after he had started the Jazz At The Philharmonic here in Los Angeles. And I did some things for him. I did some things for the Messner Brothers on their label; I don't remember the name of the label, but anyway...

Right. And we did some things for them after we had added J.D. King, the tenor player. Some of those things I wish I could take back, because we used to do some real show business type stuff on the stage, but it didn't come off too well on the record! [LAUGHS]

We had a thing we used to call "Hollywood"(?) where we just honked and went on, you know, back and forth. J.D. had made that thing more or less famous when he was with Andy Kirk, him and Jimmy Forrest, the great Jimmy Forrest, tenor player out of the original
McShann band. They used to do this...did it with Andy Kirk. So Howard had us doing that bit. Show business, you know. Pushing each other from the microphone, with all that type of thing.
Nobody was lying on their back on the floor, though.
No, we didn't get on the floor, no-no, and walk the bar and all of that bit. But it was...
